title: Fasting
definition: Fasting is the voluntary setting aside of food or other lawful comforts for a time in order to seek God with focused prayer and dependence.
summary: Fasting expresses hunger for God, humility before Him, and dependence on His grace.
christFocus: Jesus fasted, taught about fasting, and calls His people to seek the Father with sincerity rather than religious display.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Fasting is a biblical practice of humbling the body and focusing the heart before God. It is often joined with prayer, repentance, seeking guidance, grief, or urgent need.

Fasting is not a way to manipulate God or prove spiritual superiority. Jesus warned against fasting for public attention. True fasting turns the heart toward the Father.

Fasting can reveal what controls the heart. By setting aside a lawful comfort, believers confess that they need God more than daily provision and desire His will above their own comfort.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many believers live distracted, overfed, and spiritually dull. Fasting matters because it creates space for focused dependence, repentance, prayer, and renewed hunger for God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Fast wisely and humbly as health allows. Use the time to pray, read Scripture, repent, and seek God. Do not fast for attention; fast before the Father who sees in secret.
